headline: Google’s Finland AI Plan Still Waits On The Hardware Proof
deck: The supported record shows a two-year €13 billion AI-infrastructure commitment in Finland; it does not yet show the site, grid or power-delivery details that would prove operating capacity.
body: Google’s Finnish AI buildout is visible in the record first as a money clock. The Google record names a 9 September announcement for a two-year €13 billion investment in AI infrastructure in Finland. That is enough to treat the plan as a dated capital commitment, but not enough to treat it as delivered compute capacity. [E1]

Reuters carried the same Finland AI-infrastructure investment story in a separate public record. The supplied Reuters fragment is only an investment slug, so it corroborates the existence of a reported Finland AI-infrastructure investment without carrying the power-contract mechanics or construction details. The article therefore cannot rest on the 22-year Fortum agreement, plant-output share, Loviisa extension point or any exact nuclear-delivery term. [E2]

The hardware question is narrower than the first version made it. A two-year investment announcement can start procurement, site work and utility coordination, but the fragment in hand does not identify Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos or Vaala. It also does not show grid improvements, clean-energy projects, batteries, transmission connection dates or site-by-site load. [E1]

That missing layer matters because AI capacity becomes real at the interface between buildings, substations, power contracts and installed servers. The supported evidence shows a large Finnish AI-infrastructure envelope; it does not show contracted megawatts, annual energy, interconnection milestones or the share of spending that goes to accelerators rather than civil works. The boring reading is still possible: Google has announced a finance and construction envelope before the record proves operating capacity. [E1] [E2]

The economic claims should stay off the page until a fuller record carries them. The supplied Google fragment does not show a GDP estimate, a jobs estimate or the assumptions behind either figure. Those numbers may exist in the underlying announcement, but this filing can only use the captured Record fragments, and the captured fragment here is the announcement title and €13 billion figure. [E1]

The clean test is now explicit. Evidence that would strengthen the capacity claim would be a dated utility or grid document showing connection capacity and service dates, a construction filing tied to a named data-center site, or a power-purchase record with megawatts, delivery period and counterparty obligations. Without that, the supported story is a two-year €13 billion Finland AI-infrastructure commitment and a separate Reuters investment record, not proof that new AI compute is already physically available. [E1] [E2]
